subject: Mathematics
title: Probability
summary: Probability of an event = favourable outcomes / total equally likely outcomes. The addition rule handles 'or', the multiplication rule handles 'and'.
Conditional probability P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) leads to the total probability theorem and Bayes' theorem — a JEE favourite.
A random variable assigns numbers to outcomes; its distribution has a mean (expectation) and variance. The binomial distribution models n independent trials with success probability p.

formulas.name: Addition rule
formulas.formula: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B);  mutually exclusive: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B)

formulas.name: Multiplication rule and independence
formulas.formula: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B|A);  independent ⇔ P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B)
formulas.mistake: Mutually exclusive events (with non-zero probabilities) are never independent.

formulas.name: Total probability
formulas.formula: P(A) = Σ P(Eᵢ)P(A|Eᵢ)  for a partition E₁, …, Eₙ

formulas.name: Bayes' theorem
formulas.when: Reverse probability — which cause produced the result.

formulas.name: Random variable
formulas.formula: mean μ = E(X) = Σ xᵢpᵢ;  variance σ² = Σ xᵢ²pᵢ − μ²

formulas.name: Binomial distribution
formulas.formula: P(X = r) = C(n, r) pʳ qⁿ⁻ʳ (q = 1 − p);  mean np;  variance npq

formulas.name: Common sample spaces
formulas.formula: two dice: 36 outcomes;  three coins: 8;  a pack: 52 cards (4 suits × 13)

formulas.name: Odds
formulas.formula: odds in favour of A = P(A) : P(A′)

examples.title: Bayes
examples.problem: Bag I has 3 red, 2 black; bag II has 2 red, 3 black. A bag is picked at random and a red ball drawn. P(it came from bag I)?

examples.title: Binomial
examples.problem: A coin is tossed 4 times. P(exactly 2 heads)?

examples.title: At least one six
examples.problem: P(at least one six in 3 throws of a die)?

examples.title: Expectation
examples.problem: Expected value of a fair die roll?

topics.title: Events
topics.explain: Sample space S, events as subsets; mutually exclusive (no common outcome), exhaustive (union = S), independent (one doesn't affect the other), complementary.

topics.title: Using P&C
topics.explain: For cards, committees or arrangements, count favourable and total cases with combinations. E.g. P(2 aces in 2 cards) = ⁴C₂/⁵²C₂ = 1/221.

topics.title: Independent vs mutually exclusive
topics.explain: Independent: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B). Mutually exclusive: P(A ∩ B) = 0. If A and B are independent, so are A′ and B, A and B′, A′ and B′.

topics.title: Geometric probability
topics.explain: When outcomes are points in a region, probability = favourable length/area/volume ÷ total.

topics.title: Problems on 'without replacement'
topics.explain: Probabilities change after each draw; use conditional probabilities or combinations directly.

topics.title: Bayes' strategy
topics.explain: List causes (bags, machines, persons) with prior probabilities, find P(result | cause) for each, compute total probability of the result, then divide the required term by the total.

ratta: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
Bayes = one path ÷ total of all paths.
